subject: Post-demo: inference economics & feature-level cost sketch (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@mediqhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 14:02 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: inference economics & feature-level cost sketch (next steps)

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a lightweight unit-econ sketch to make the discussion actionable for your finance and product execs.

Call attendees (as I captured):
- Sarah Lin (MediQ)
- Daniel Park (MediQ, PM)
- Marissa Cole (Redwood)
- Ben Carter (Redwood)
- Monica Patel (Redwood, Solutions)

What you confirmed on the call:
- Primary production feature: "Smart Triage" (triage suggestions + short summaries) and a secondary "Patient Summary" feature for clinician notes.
- Active user base: ~50k MAU; initial feature adoption target ~20% (10k DAU peak scenario).
- Rough target latency: 150–250ms p95 for Smart Triage; auditable logs required.
- Budget posture: finance indicated an initial monthly inference budget range of $30k–$60k while they evaluate ROI; they asked for a $/1M tokens target to compare to their internal model.
- Security: SOC2 + isolated tenant important; they also asked about VPC/private deployment options (we noted Redwood Private).

Initial unit-econ sketch (very rough, for alignment):
- Assumptions: Smart Triage average payload ~600 tokens per invocation (prompt + response), Patient Summary ~1,200 tokens.
- Usage scenarios (monthly):
  * Conservative: 100k invocations / month (10k DAU * 10 uses) => 60M tokens (Smart Triage)
  * Target: 1.0M invocations / month => 600M tokens
  * Aggressive: 1.5M invocations / month => 900M tokens
- Target $/1M tokens (what finance asked for): you said they'd prefer to see a target in the $300–$500 range to compare vs current estimates.

Example cost math (at $450 per 1M tokens):
- Target (1.0M invocations): 600M tokens => 600 * $450 = $270k / month (note: that is raw inference bill to Redwood; we would propose pricing structures below to get to your budget envelope)
- Conservative (100k invocations): 60M tokens => 60 * $450 = $27k / month
- Aggressive (1.5M invocations): 900M tokens => 900 * $450 = $405k / month

Feature-level $/feature metric (monthly):
- Smart Triage at 1.0M invocations => inference cost ~ $270k / month => $0.27 per invocation (raw inference cost)
- If you monetize at $3.00 ARPU per invocation-equivalent (example) => gross margin before infra & ops ~ 90% at these numbers (this is illustrative — we'll need your revenue per feature to compute CAC payback).

CAC / payback back-of-envelope (ask from your finance):
- If CAC per new clinic / account is $6k and monthly incremental revenue from feature is $1,500 => payback ~ 4 months.
- If we structure a pilot (8–12 weeks) with credits + usage cap we can accelerate adoption and get telemetry to validate these numbers.

Requested next steps (let me know if the phrasing below looks good):
1) Sarah: confirm a realistic 3-month token ramp (conservative / target / aggressive) and your expected ARPU/monetization per clinician or per encounter.
2) Ben: can you draft two pricing options for MediQ — (A) usage-led list + pilot credits, (B) reserved capacity (committed monthly tokens) with a lower unit price and a 12‑month commitment — and include an example invoice at the three usage scenarios?
3) Monica: please provision a trial tenant (redwood private trial or hosted) and set up telemetry we'll need to capture tokens per invocation and latency breakdowns.
4) I will prepare the one-pager for their CFO showing unit-econ sensitivity (we can attach the XLS I ran).

Attached: metiq-inference-snapshot.xlsx (very rough calc).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m follow-up with your finance/ops next week.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@mediqhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@mediqhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 09:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: inference economics & feature-level cost sketch (next steps)

Thanks Marissa — appreciated the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our side so you can refine the one-pager: 

- Token/usage guidance: Daniel and I sketched conservative -> target -> stretch as follows: conservative = 50k invocations/month, target = 800k, stretch = 1.3M. Those are per-feature (Smart Triage) numbers — Patient Summary would be ~30% of that.
- Budget: finance is comfortable starting with an evaluation budget of $35k/month, with potential to expand if the ROI signals are strong; they'd like an execution plan that gives them visibility into month-to-month unit cost.
- Commitment appetite: we're open to a 6-month pilot with a capped committed amount if you can provide a unit price that scales down between committed and overage usage.
- Security: SOC2 + isolated tenant requirement is real; Daniel will follow up with the info sec checklist.

Can you include a scenario where committed pricing (e.g., a 6-month $/1M token committed block) sits at roughly 60% of the pay-as-you-go unit price? That'll help us evaluate.

Finally — yes to the 8–12 week pilot. We'll need a concise SOW and a 1-page exec memo for our CFO.

Regards,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Product, MediQ Health
sarah.lin@mediqhealth.com
+1 (617) 555-0199

Attachment: mediq-pilot-request.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 17 May 2028 08:23 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: inference economics & feature-level cost sketch (next steps)

Ben / Monica — forwarding Sarah's clarifications. Key asks: committed pricing option ~40% lower unit than payg (Sarah asked for ~60% of payg; let's show both 40% and 60% comps), and a 6-month capped pilot structure at ~$35k/month initial spend.

Action items for pricing doc (please include in the one-pager + example invoice):
- Baseline pay-as-you-go unit price (per 1M tokens) and sample math for conservative/target/stretch scenarios using Sarah's ranges (50k / 800k / 1.3M invocations).
- Committed block option for 6 months: show price at -40% and -60% off payg, with clear overage rules.
- A reserved capacity example where a committed token pool (e.g., 2B tokens/month) gives an even lower unit and how model fallback would work if they exceed KV cache expectations.
- Recommend pilot credits (we typically propose 25–50% credits for 8–12 week pilots).
- Call out telemetry requirements (tokens per invocation, latency p95, percent cache hits, per-route cost) so Monica can instrument correctly.

Ben: can you drop a first draft of the two pricing options by EOD today? Monica: can you confirm trial tenant provisioning ETA and what we can provide for log-level telemetry during pilot?

Thanks — I'll consolidate and send to Sarah + Daniel and include a CFO-facing one-pager.

—
Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

1) PAYG structure with 3 unit-price bands and example invoices for Sarah's three usage scenarios.
2) Committed 6-month structure with both -40% and -60% pricing comps and a simple overage floor.
3) Pilot credit recommendation (we'll show 30% credits by default and a stretched 50% option).

Monica — if you can confirm telemetry keys and trial tenant ETA, I'll finalize the numbers and share the one-pager.
